designed_by: Claude (the AI coding assistant), written in parallel with gemini-4-carbon's designs so the two can be compared and merged
principle: Everything that happens in the product is an event on entities. The room, the map and the diary are views of that state. Nothing is drawn that is not the projection of an entity, a link or an event.

scopes.shared: The base. Things in the world. Supabase. Every Gemi reads it; checked facts may be added. Never a person.
scopes.private: One student's side. Lives in that student's browser. The Gemi, its beliefs, its room, its ledger, its diary.
scopes.pairwise: A name card. Each side stores its own copy. No central list of who knows whom.

update_rule.state: position p in [-1,1], halo h in (0,1], start p=0, h=1
update_rule.step: e = evidence direction in [-1,1] from the rubric, c = Decisions confidence. k = weight * c * h. p = p + k*(e - p). h = h * (1 - 0.5*weight*c).
update_rule.contradiction: if |e - p| > 0.8 and h < 0.5 then h = min(1, h + 0.15): it becomes less sure, not more.
update_rule.silence: h grows 0.02 per week without evidence on that axis.
update_rule.undo: mark the event undone and recompute from the log.

gap_rule.formula: score(resource) = sum over needs(weight(need) * serves(resource, need)) + 0.5 * sum over axes(halo(axis) * informs(resource, axis))
gap_rule.plan: pick the trip whose expected score per star is highest; always include one pair of finds that contrast on the widest-halo axis
gap_rule.example: Needs: find_my_people 0.8. Halo widest on collaboration. Plan: Clubs house (1 group event, 1 solo-friendly one), 3 stars, reason shown to the student in one sentence.

self_use_modes.idea: The Gemi has its own purse. Before spending it asks one question: what is this token best used for? It may think, act, or make. Each mode sits under governance that is enforced in code, not in the prompt.

modes.what: decide what to do with the stars it has: plan the day, seal a prediction, reflect, write the diary
modes.limits: capped share of the for-itself purse; every plan states its reason in one sentence the student can read

modes.what: call a registered tool: go out for resources, check a claim, ask an agent, meet a Gemi, arrange or decorate its room
modes.side_effects: only what the tool declares (which entities it reads and writes, in which scope)
modes.limits: cost charged before the call; daily caps per tool; reversible tools run freely, anything that touches the student's real life always asks first

modes.what: build something new for itself: a new room item, a small widget, a new routine made of existing tools
modes.side_effects: a proposal, never a direct install
modes.limits: it writes to a fixed contract (an item factory or a declarative recipe of existing tools), never free code with network or data access

governance: Registry: a tool that is not registered cannot be called. Each entry declares reads, writes, scope, cost, whether it is reversible, and its confirm rule.
Budget: stars are charged from the right purse before the call; no stars, no call. Real token usage is recorded next to it.
Scope: a tool that writes to the shared base cannot carry anything from the private side into it. The outbox gate checks every outgoing message.
Stage: tools unlock by stage, on measured conditions.

Make pipeline: 1. contract check by static scan (no imports, no network, no storage, no DOM, size limit); 2. dry run in isolation; 3. a Decisions check that it does what it says and carries nothing private; 4. the student approves; 5. installed as revocable, with its source, cost and author recorded.
Log: every call, refusal and approval is an event the student can read. Refusals are shown, not hidden.
Kill switch: the student can pause the Gemi's autonomy or remove anything it made.
self_use_modes.today: think and act are built for real. make is built for one kind: the Gemi asks gemini-4-neon for a new room item to the item contract; the pipeline above decides whether it is installed.
